sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Chanhassen, MN?
sections.html:
A Chanhassen homeowner can list on the open market, sell privately, or take a direct offer from a cash buyer. With the highest home values of any of the four cities in this area, the gap between a polished listing and an as-is sale can be large, so it pays to compare.

  • A full listing makes sense when the house is updated and you have time for showings.
  • A private sale suits owners who have a buyer in mind, such as a neighbor or relative.
  • A cash buyer fits an estate house, a property with a failing septic system, or a seller who must move before the school year or a job start.

Owners occupy 84.1% of Chanhassen's homes, so most neighbors a buyer meets are long-term residents rather than tenants.

sections.h2: Where is Chanhassen, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Chanhassen is mostly in Carver County, about 15 miles southwest of Minneapolis, with a small eastern piece reaching into Hennepin County. The city covers 22.88 square miles, of which 20.44 are land and 2.44 are water. U.S. Highway 212 and Minnesota Highways 5 and 41 are the main routes.

The first settlers arrived in 1852, mostly German farm families. The name comes from a Dakota word for the sugar maple, and it became official in 1858. Chanhassen merged with its township and became a city on May 8, 1967, with about 4,200 residents. Population has risen 123.5% since 1990. The Minnesota Landscape Arboretum, Paisley Park, Chanhassen Dinner Theatres and the headquarters of Life Time sit here, and the National Weather Service's Twin Cities forecast office is in town. Five public beaches on Lake Ann, Lake Minnewashta and Lotus Lake and 70 miles of trails give the listing photos plenty to work with.

sections.h2: How do the housing numbers compare to nearby cities?
sections.html:
Among Brooklyn Park, Burnsville, Chanhassen and Chaska, Chanhassen has the priciest homes. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $566,300 for 2020-2024, against $336,200 in Brooklyn Park.

About 64.1% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and only 2.9% of residents live in poverty. The 2020 census put the rental vacancy rate at 8.5%, compared with 5.5% in Brooklyn Park and 4.0% in Chaska, which is worth knowing if you are pricing a rental house.

sections.h2: Who is likely to buy a house in Chanhassen?
sections.html:
Buyers here skew toward established families. The 2020 census found a median age of 40.9, with 64.9% of households headed by married couples and 36.8% including children under 18. Per capita income is $76,879, and 90.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so listings tend to come from owners with long tenure and substantial equity.

Commutes average 22.3 minutes, and about 15.4% of residents are 65 or older, which feeds a steady supply of downsizers. If you are selling an inherited house, expect the buyer pool to compare it with updated listings at much higher prices, so an as-is price will reflect the work the buyer takes on rather than the neighborhood's median.

Most of Chanhassen lies in Eastern Carver County Schools, District 112. Typical attendance for those students runs through Bluff Creek and Chanhassen Elementary, Pioneer Ridge Middle School and Chanhassen High School.

The northern sections belong to the Minnetonka School District, District 276, with students usually attending Clear Springs or Excelsior Elementary, Minnetonka Middle School West and Minnetonka High School. Private options in the downtown area include Chapel Hill Academy and St. Hubert Catholic School. The district line can run through a neighborhood, so confirm the specific address with the district before it goes into a listing.

sections.h2: Do septic systems and wells affect a Chanhassen sale?
sections.html:
Yes, for the part of the city that is not on city sewer or water. About 3.9% of residents live in areas the Census classifies as rural, and rural parcels are the likeliest to have private systems. Minnesota law has two separate disclosures for them.

  • Sewage: before signing a purchase agreement, a seller must tell the buyer in writing whether sewage goes to a permitted facility or to a subsurface sewage treatment system, and attach any prior inspection report (Minnesota Statutes section 115.55, subdivision 6). A seller who knew of a system and failed to disclose it can be liable for compliance costs for two years after closing.
  • Wells: the seller must disclose known wells in writing, and the deed needs a well statement or a certificate with a $54 fee (section 103I.235). Liability for an undisclosed well can run six years from closing.

Carver County lists the subsurface sewage treatment disclosure as required on all property transfers. If you are unsure what is buried in the yard, ask the city's building staff and your title company early.

sections.h2: Can you rent your Chanhassen house short-term before you sell?
sections.html:
Only with a license. Chanhassen's ordinance, in effect since January 1, 2023, requires a license for any property rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days, even if it happens only a couple of times a year. Month-to-month leases do not trigger it.

The license costs $200 a year, is renewed by February 1, and requires a Minnesota state lodging license. License terms set the maximum number of overnight guests and vehicles and require compliance with the nuisance ordinance, including a 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. limit on amplified sound. Three notices of violation within 365 days mean revocation, and the owner cannot hold a short-term rental license again for seven years. Neighbors can report problems to a 24/7 hotline at 952-260-4995. An owner who is listing a house should remove any active short-term listing before the first showing.

Carver County Land Records and Vitals, at 600 East 4th Street in Chaska, records deeds for most of the city. Office hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, and the main line is 952-361-1930. Parcels in the Hennepin County portion are recorded through Hennepin County instead, so check the county named on your tax statement.

A Carver deed package needs the recording fee, state deed tax, a $5 agricultural conservation fee, a certificate of real estate value when consideration is over $3,000, the well information, the sewage treatment disclosure, a complete legal description, a complete notary acknowledgment, a drafted-by statement and a send-tax-statements-to line. The recorder cannot provide legal advice or choose a form for you, so rely on your title company or attorney. Deed tax is imposed by section 287.21 at 0.33% of net consideration.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Chanhassen house with a septic problem?
faqs.a: Many will, since they buy as-is and price in the repair. You still must disclose what you know about the system in writing, and attach any inspection report you hold.

faqs.q: Which county records my Chanhassen deed?
faqs.a: Carver County for nearly all of the city, and Hennepin County for the small eastern portion. Your tax statement shows the county that applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to list my Chanhassen home on Airbnb while it is for sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Any rental under 30 consecutive days needs a $200 annual city license and a Minnesota lodging license. Operating without one risks enforcement.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed tax on a Chanhassen sale?
faqs.a: It is 0.33% of the net consideration. On a $566,300 sale, the median value Census reports for the city, that is roughly $1,869.

faqs.q: What school district is a Chanhassen house in?
faqs.a: Most addresses are in District 112, Eastern Carver County Schools. Northern parts are in District 276, Minnetonka. Verify by address.
